intro: Professionals and everyday users convert psi (psi) to kilopascals (kPa) when working across imperial and metric standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One pounds per square inch equals 6.894757 kilopascals, while 1 kilopascal equals 0.145038 psi. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between psi and kPa. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many kilopascals (kPa) are in 1 pounds per square inch (psi)?
faqs.answer: There are 6.89475729 kilopascals (kPa) in 1 pounds per square inch (psi), which rounds to 6.8948 kPa for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 kilopascal equals 0.145038 psi.

faqs.question: How do I convert psi to kilopascals (psi to kPa)?
faqs.answer: To convert psi to kilopascals, use the formula: kPa = psi × 6.89475729. For example, converting 35 psi gives 241.3165 kPa.

faqs.question: What is 35 psi in kilopascals?
faqs.answer: 35 psi (psi) equals exactly 241.3165 kilopascals (kPa) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
